title: Pre-Capstone: Design Your Data
story: Before you build the ultimate capstone, let's practice designing data systems from scratch. Given a domain — a library catalog, a fitness tracker, a recipe box — what structs, enums, and collections would you choose? Let's work through a complete example together, then you design your own.
why: Software design starts with data modeling — choosing the right types, structs, and collections before writing a single line of logic ensures your code is organized from day one.
analogy: Designing a data model is like planning a city — you identify the buildings (structs), the roads connecting them (collections), and the zoning rules (types). A well-planned city is easy to navigate; a poorly planned one leads to chaos. The same is true for your code.
try_it: Implement the full RecipeBox: when adding a recipe, iterate over its tags and update the by_tag Map. Write `find_by_tag` that returns all recipe names for a given tag. Write `find_quick_meals` that returns recipes with cook_time < 30. Then design your OWN domain: a game inventory, a music library, or a contact book. Define the types, choose collections, and explain why you chose each one.
tips: Start with nouns (entities) → then fields (properties) → then collections (relationships) → then operations (functions)
Use Map for lookups (ISBN→Book), Vec for ordered lists (loan history), Set for uniqueness (tags)
A single entity often needs multiple collections — a Book appears in the catalog Map AND the loan history Vec
common_mistakes: Skipping the design phase and coding immediately — 5 minutes of planning saves 50 minutes of rewriting
Choosing collections based on convenience rather than access patterns — always ask 'how will I query this data?'
Overcomplicating: start with 2-3 fields per struct and expand — you can always add fields later
